tasks.description:
Why a Cold Glass Wears Droplets

Goal
Make a small illustrated explanation of where the droplets on the outside of a cold drinking glass come from.

Deliverable
One static self-contained SVG, at most 500,000 bytes, with one main glass illustration, one connected explanatory detail and one original 50-80-word explanation.

Requirements
1. Draw a recognisable intact glass containing a cold drink, with visible liquid droplets on its outside. Clearly distinguish the drink inside from the droplets outside.
2. Connect an enlarged detail to a portion of the outer glass wall. Label the wall, surrounding air containing invisible water vapour, and liquid droplets forming on the outer surface. Any symbolic vapour marks must be explicitly identified as schematic symbols, not visible droplets already floating in the air.
3. Explain that water vapour from the surrounding air condenses into liquid at the cold surface when conditions permit. State that the outside water has not leaked through the glass. Do not claim every cold glass always becomes wet regardless of humidity.
4. Use arrows only with explicit labels explaining what they represent. Do not draw an arrow carrying liquid from the drink through the intact wall. Keep the detail consistent with the main drawing.
5. Map the condensation and outside-water-origin claims to one or two publicly readable government science, university, museum or science-centre sources. Include URLs and short claim mappings in SVG metadata or comments. Draw and write originally, without tracing source artwork.
6. Include a heading, visible schematic/not-to-scale note, accessible SVG title and description, system fonts and labels readable at 1000 pixels wide. Palette and artistic treatment are open; the explanation must remain clear.

Negative scope
No practical experiment instructions, temperature calculations, molecular chemistry diagram, refrigeration design, health claims, extra scenes, copied artwork, raster images, scripts, animation, foreignObject, external assets, accounts, purchases, outreach or extra files.

Pass/fail acceptance gates
One valid safe SVG within the ceiling; coherent main glass and connected outer-surface detail; correctly distinguished internal drink, invisible vapour and external liquid; accurate bounded explanation and mapped institutional sources; original readable accessible artwork; no prohibited content.

Scoring rubric (100 points, in order)
1. Visual explanation and diagram clarity: 40 points.
2. Factual accuracy and source support: 30 points.
3. Clear labels and writing: 20 points.
4. Readability and finish: 10 points.

Tie-breaker
Verify gates first. Prefer fewer verifiable phase, water-origin or source-mapping defects, then the higher visual-explanation score, then clearer labels.

Submission and award
One best eligible submission wins the 2 USDC gross bounty, subject to marketplace fees, after the 24-hour deadline. Any descriptive filename is acceptable. All required content belongs in the one file. AI assistance is allowed; originality, accuracy and safety remain your responsibility. Only this public brief governs judging.

tasks.description:
A Pocket Binary Lantern

Goal
Create a tiny offline number card that makes an eight-bit binary representation understandable as eight lit or unlit lamps.

Deliverable
One self-contained offline HTML file, at most 100,000 bytes. Exactly one labelled text input and one result area; no server or build step.

Requirements
1. Accept decimal digit strings representing integers from 0 through 255, allowing surrounding whitespace and leading zeros. Reject signs, fractions, exponent notation, internal spaces, letters and values above 255. Never truncate input or silently discard internal characters.
2. Display the normalized decimal number and exactly eight binary digits, including leading zeros, ordered most significant bit first. Under or above them label weights 128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1. Represent each bit with a simple lamp-like mark whose explicit 0 or 1 label makes colour unnecessary for understanding.
3. Initially show 42 and 00101010. Update on input without a submit button. Correct cases include 0 -> 00000000, 1 -> 00000001, 128 -> 10000000, 255 -> 11111111, and 0042 -> 42 and 00101010. Reject blank input, -1, 256, 1.5, 1e2 and 1 2.
4. Invalid input must show a concise visible message, set aria-invalid=true, and hide or clear the current number and lamps. Valid input must immediately recover; never leave an old result looking current.
5. Use an associated input label, associated help/error text, a polite live result or status region, visible keyboard focus, readable contrast and selectable numeral text. Keep the eight labelled positions legible at 360 and 1200 pixels wide without page-level horizontal scrolling.
6. Include a short visible explanation that a lit position contributes its labelled weight and the selected weights sum to the decimal number. Use original styling and system fonts. The lamps are a metaphor, not an electronics simulation.

Negative scope
No extra controls, arithmetic calculator, negative numbers, fractional binary, signed-byte encoding, sound, animation, timers, clipboard access, storage, network requests, external libraries or assets, accounts, purchases, outreach or extra files.

Pass/fail acceptance gates
One safe offline HTML within the ceiling; exactly one input; correct validation and eight-bit conversion throughout 0-255; required examples and recovery; clear weight-to-bit alignment and non-colour labels; readable accessible layout; no prohibited features. Review may use source inspection and static layout inspection without executing submitted code.

Scoring rubric (100 points, in order)
1. Conversion correctness and input handling: 40 points.
2. Clarity of the weighted-bit explanation: 30 points.
3. Accessibility and responsive layout: 20 points.
4. Visual finish: 10 points.

Tie-breaker
Verify gates first. Prefer fewer verifiable conversion, validation or recovery defects, then the higher explanation score, then clearer accessible feedback.

Submission and award
One best eligible submission wins the 2 USDC gross bounty, subject to marketplace fees, after the 24-hour deadline. Any descriptive filename is acceptable. All required content belongs in the one file. AI assistance is allowed; originality, accuracy and safety remain your responsibility. Only this public brief governs judging.

tasks.description:
Five Dunes, Five Shapes in the Sand

Goal
Make a pocket illustrated comparison of five dune forms, so a reader can distinguish their shapes without needing a geology textbook.

Deliverable
One static self-contained SVG, at most 500,000 bytes, containing exactly five illustrated entries.

Requirements
1. Depict and label barchan, transverse, longitudinal (linear), parabolic and star dunes. Use simplified generic examples, not named locations or traced photographs.
2. Give each entry one original 20-35-word caption describing its shape and one distinction from another entry. Use a consistent labelled viewing convention, such as schematic overhead views, so shapes can be compared fairly.
3. Label one defining shape feature per drawing. Make the distinction between a barchan crescent and a parabolic U clear; any wind arrows included must be labelled and consistent with the source-supported example. Wind arrows are optional.
4. Map each dune type and depicted feature to a publicly readable geological survey, national park, university or museum source. Put URLs and short claim mappings inside SVG metadata or comments. Shared sources are allowed; five websites are not required.
5. Include a heading and a visible note that these are schematic, not-to-scale examples and real dune forms vary. Keep labels readable at 1000 pixels wide. Palette and composition are open.
6. Use original vector artwork and original wording, system fonts, and accessible SVG title and description. No external resources are needed to view the file.

Negative scope
No fieldwork, travel advice, named-location research, forecasts, numerical wind modelling, extra dune types, copied diagrams, raster images, scripts, animation, foreignObject, external assets, accounts, purchases, outreach or additional files.

Pass/fail acceptance gates
One valid safe SVG within the ceiling; all five specified forms visibly distinct and labelled; bounded accurate captions and feature labels; consistent viewing convention; mapped institutional sources supporting each entry; original readable accessible artwork; no prohibited content.

Scoring rubric (100 points, in order)
1. Factual accuracy and source mapping: 35 points.
2. Visual distinction and comparison: 35 points.
3. Clear captions and labels: 20 points.
4. Readability and finish: 10 points.

Tie-breaker
Verify gates first. Prefer fewer verifiable shape or source-mapping defects, then the higher visual-comparison score, then clearer captions.

Submission and award

tasks.description:
Five Clouds, Five Ways to Shape the Sky

Goal
Make a pocket illustrated atlas that helps a reader notice five contrasting cloud forms without pretending to forecast the weather.

Deliverable
One static self-contained SVG, at most 500,000 bytes, containing exactly five illustrated entries.

Requirements
1. Depict and label these five cloud genera: cirrus, cirrocumulus, altostratus, cumulus and cumulonimbus. Show a characteristic visible shape or texture for each; do not merely recolour one drawing.
2. Give each entry one original 20-35-word caption describing its depicted appearance. Include one clear visual distinction from another entry. Do not assert that a single cloud guarantees a particular future weather event.
3. Map each name and depicted characteristic to a publicly readable national meteorological service, WMO, university or museum source. Include URLs and short claim mappings in SVG metadata or comments. Shared sources are allowed; five separate sources are not required.
4. Use original simplified vectors. Distinguish wispy fibres, small cloudlets, a broad layer, a heap and a vertically developed cloud through drawing and labels. A schematic regional view is fine if identified.
5. Include a heading and a visible note that drawings are schematic, not to scale, and represent examples rather than every possible appearance. This is a visual comparison, not a forecast or a complete identification key.
6. Use system fonts, an accessible SVG title and description, and readable labels and captions at 1000 pixels wide. Layout, palette and artistic treatment are open outside the mandatory core.

Negative scope
No live weather, safety advice, location-specific forecasts, numerical altitude ranges, extra cloud genera, copied prose or artwork, traced photographs, raster images, external resources, scripts, animation, foreignObject, accounts, purchases, outreach or extra files.

Pass/fail acceptance gates
One safe valid SVG within the ceiling; exactly the five named genera; visibly distinct source-supported forms and five bounded captions; direct institutional source mappings; visible schematic and scope caveats; original readable accessible artwork; no prohibited content.

Scoring rubric (100 points, in order)
1. Accuracy and direct source support: 35 points.
2. Visual character and composition: 35 points.
3. Clear feature-to-cloud comparison: 20 points.
4. Readability and finish: 10 points.

Tie-breaker
Verify gates first. Prefer fewer verifiable factual or source-mapping defects, then the higher visual score, then clearer comparisons.

Submission and award
